name: Fibular Aplasia-Ectrodactyly Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Fibular Aplasia-Ectrodactyly Syndrome

criteria.description: Congenital absence or hypoplasia of the fibula
Split hand/foot malformation characterized by median clefts and missing central digits
Delayed ossification of tarsal and metatarsal bones on imaging
Presence of additional limb anomalies such as syndactyly or clinodactyly

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital fibular aplasia or hypoplasia combined with ectrodactyly of the hands and/or feet
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by radiographic findings; genetic testing may assist but no definitive gene identified

searchTerms: small or absent lower leg bone

imaging: Radiographic absence or hypoplasia of the fibula
Split hand/foot malformation visible on X-ray
Delayed ossification of tarsal and metatarsal bones
genetic: No definitive causative gene identified; possible sporadic or autosomal dominant inheritance with variable expressivity
other: Clinical examination revealing limb malformations at birth

distinguishingFeatures: Often familial with known genetic mutations (e.g., SHFM1, SHFM3)
Fibular aplasia or hypoplasia without ectrodactyly

redFlags: Severe limb deformities causing functional impairment
Progressive limb length discrepancy leading to gait abnormalities
Associated congenital anomalies requiring multidisciplinary management
references: Hunter AGW, et al. The fibular aplasia-ectrodactyly syndrome: clinical and radiological features. J Med Genet. 1985
